findings.title: LIMIT MAX_LOOKUP_IDS can truncate the batch and under-price peers
findings.problem: The IN list carries up to two candidates per requested id (resource_id and arn), so GROUP BY line_item_resource_id can return up to 200 groups against LIMIT 100. ORDER BY cost DESC drops the cheapest, while the unpartitioned totalCost/groupCount windows still describe all groups, so costs, pricedCount and totalCost become mutually inconsistent. §6.4's claim that the page is the whole set is false.
findings.fix: Emit `LIMIT curIds.size()` (the candidate count) instead of MAX_LOOKUP_IDS; restate the §6.4 bullet; change criterion 22 to assert the LIMIT equals the candidate-list size and add a test where one requested id has two candidates that both return a CUR group.

findings.title: A requested id that is itself a poisoned short identifier gets an arbitrary resource's cost
findings.where: §6.6 algorithm steps 3-5; §5.2 'Why the matching is sound' point 3
findings.problem: Step 4 drops the poisoned candidate but still resolves the requested id to 'the row it resolves to' using index's ACTIVE-wins tie-break, which §5.2 point 4 itself calls wrong for two different resources. The surviving candidate is then one of the two resources' unique ARNs, picked arbitrarily, so a confident but possibly wrong cost is rendered - exactly what FR-11 forbids. Reachable on the inventory-plane path, where peer ids ARE resource_id, and present in the demo fixtures (RDS db:xammer-prod vs EKS cluster/xammer-prod).
findings.fix: Apply the poison check to the requested id before the row lookup: if the requested id is itself claimed by two rows with different ARNs, emit no candidates and list it in `ambiguous`; do not fall through to a row. Add an acceptance criterion for curIdentifiers(acct, ["shared"]) returning no candidates and listing it ambiguous.

findings.title: A failed /resource-identities call renders the benign 'not in the topology' state, permanently
findings.where: §8.3 candidate loop; §8.5 state 2 and the 'identities lands in 1a' sentence; §9.2 rows 5-6; §9.3
findings.problem: readShape in curInsightsApi.ts never throws - it returns null for any body that fails the shape predicate, including 404/409/502/400. So a failed identities query resolves successfully with data === null, isError is false, candidates is [], and §8.5's ordering renders state 2 ('This resource is not in the account topology') with no retry control, made permanent by useCurInsight's retry: false. The 400-specific console.warn is also unimplementable because readShape discards res.status.
findings.fix: Give fetchResourceIdentities a throwing contract (throw on non-2xx with the status in the message, throw on unexpected shape) and type ConnectivityFetchers.identities as Promise<ResourceIdentities>; additionally require identity !== null for state 2 and route a settled null to state 1a. Add a criterion: a rejecting identities fetcher renders state 1a with Try again and never the 'not in the topology' sentence.

findings.title: Three sections give three different rules for membership of `ambiguous`
findings.problem: §5.2 says both colliding ids are ambiguous and neither is priced, then says each keeps its unique ARN so the common case prices. §6.6 step 5 lists an id as ambiguous only when its candidate set is empty. Criterion 26 says both ids appear in ambiguous. The three cannot all hold, and the difference is user-visible: `ambiguous` renders as 'cost not attributable to this resource alone' instead of a figure.
findings.fix: Adopt the narrow rule - an id is ambiguous iff it ends up with no usable candidate - and rewrite §5.2 point 3's last two sentences and criterion 26 to match, alongside the new criterion from finding 2.

findings.title: The cache key needs a resolved period but the handler builds it from the raw, unvalidated parameter
findings.where: §6.4 handler sketch and the 'period is written explicitly and resolved' bullet
findings.problem: parsePeriod (which defaults null to now and rejects blank/2026-13) runs inside withSource, after costsCacheKey would have been called with the raw string. So the key builder must either re-implement parsePeriod - two resolutions of 'now', which can straddle a month boundary - or write an unresolved value into the key, defeating isOpenMonth, which parses period= back off it.
findings.fix: Make withSourceKeyed take Function<YearMonth, String> keySuffix rather than a precomputed String, so the suffix is built from the same resolved YearMonth the query uses; correct §6.4's stated validation order to note period is still parsed inside withSourceKeyed before anything is cached or queried.

findings.title: The withSource -> withSourceKeyed refactor does break existing tests; the constructor change breaks one more
findings.where: §6.4 'the ten existing callers ... gain nothing to re-test'; §6.2; §11; criterion 33
findings.problem: CurInsightsControllerTest stubs the two-argument getOrCompute (lenient().when(insightCache.getOrCompute(anyString(), any()))) and verifies it at line ~365. If withSource delegates to withSourceKeyed, all ten endpoints invoke the three-argument overload, which is unstubbed and returns null - the test class comment says that breaks every test. Injecting ResourceIdResolver also changes the controller constructor the test calls directly, so criterion 33 cannot pass untouched.
findings.fix: Either (a) preferred: do not delegate - leave withSource on the two-argument method and let withSourceKeyed duplicate the ~8-line prologue; or (b) add CurInsightsControllerTest to §6.2's file table (new mock + constructor argument, re-stub the three-argument getOrCompute, update the verify). The constructor change is unavoidable in both, so list it either way.

findings.title: The 120 s client timeout is not the client's own choice - Spring's async timeout is exactly 120 s in prod
findings.problem: /cloudmap/graph returns a CompletableFuture, so spring.mvc.async.request-timeout applies: application.properties:246 = 120000, application-prod.properties declares 125000 then 120000 (last wins, 120 s), application-preprod.properties declares 120000 then 125000 (125 s). nginx does allow 300 s but is not the binding limit. A cold scan over 120 s races the service's 503 against the client's abort, and §12.2 item 6's remedy of raising the client timeout cannot work alone.
findings.fix: Correct §8.8 to name spring.mvc.async.request-timeout as the real ceiling (and note the duplicated declarations), set the client timeout just below it (e.g. 110_000) so failure is deterministic and client-side, and rewrite §12.2 item 6's remedy as raising the server async timeout and the client together, or warming the topology.

findings.title: Which id is sent for the focus resource is unspecified, and the obvious reading discards a known-priceable id
findings.problem: 'The focus id' reads either as the matched graph node id or as the drawer's own CUR resourceId. For Group C types the difference decides whether the focus card shows a cost at all: a load balancer's describe-path node id (my-lb) matches nothing, while the drawer's CUR id is the ARN and prices correctly. The accepted gap in §5.4 only exists under one of the two readings.
findings.fix: State the rule: the focus id is the drawer's own CUR resourceId while the trail is empty, and the peer's graph node id after a re-root; peers always travel as graph node ids. Amend §5.4 consequence (a) and criterion 5 accordingly. Still one batch query, one extra id.

findings.title: A payload with nodes but no resource nodes falls into state 2 - another false benign state
findings.problem: CloudMapService catches createNode per-resource and addVpcAndSubnetNodes runs first, so a payload can be non-empty while containing only VPC/subnet scaffolding. Those are all CONTAINER_TYPES, so resourceCount is 0, nothing matches, and the tab renders 'This resource is not in the account topology' with no retry - for a scan failure. Same class of error state 3b was added to prevent.
findings.fix: Treat `elements.length === 0 || index.resourceCount === 0` as state 1b (reload control), evaluated ahead of state 2, and add a criterion: a payload containing only VPC and Subnet nodes renders state 1b, not state 2.

findings.title: The shared fetchCloudMapGraph changes Cloud Map page behaviour, which §13 forbids
findings.problem: useCloudMap's two call sites have different, load-bearing error semantics: fetchOne counts failures and returns [] (driving the 'N of M VPCs' messages), while loadGraph throws new Error('HTTP error! status: N') whose message is rendered verbatim in graphError. §8.8 specifies the shared fetcher throws on !ok but not what the error carries, so a naive swap changes user-visible copy on another page.
findings.fix: Pin the thrown message to `HTTP error! status: ${response.status}` with a comment saying why, and record in §8.2 that each call site keeps its own timeoutMs (240 s cold / 60 s warm), forceRefresh and handling. Simpler alternative: leave useCloudMap untouched and let only the new tab use the new module, which keeps §13 honest.

findings.title: FR-7 says four unavailable states and then describes five
findings.problem: The heading and first sentence say four; the last sentence adds a fifth; §8.5 implements 1a, 1b, 2, 3a, 3b.
findings.fix: Retitle FR-7 'Five unavailable states, each with its own sentence' and list all five.

findings.title: ConnectivityFetchers.graph cannot express what §8.8 says the tab sends
findings.problem: The prop is typed (accountId, region?) => Promise<GraphElement[]>, while fetchCloudMapGraph takes an args object and the tab is specified to pass vpcId: 'ALL' and timeoutMs. The default value must therefore be an adapter, which the design never shows, leaving it open where vpcId and timeoutMs live.
findings.fix: Show the default bundle explicitly, e.g. graph: (accountId, region) => fetchCloudMapGraph({ accountId, vpcId: 'ALL', region, timeoutMs: 110_000 }).

findings.title: Criterion 4 gives the identities call a parameter it does not have
findings.problem: The criterion reads 'the identity fetcher exactly once, with the drawer's resourceId and the row's region', but /resource-identities takes only accountId and ids, and the fetcher signature has no region.
findings.fix: Split the criterion: the graph fetcher is called once with the row's region; the identity fetcher is called once with [resourceId].

findings.title: §8.1 names React 18; the repo is on React 19
findings.problem: frontend-app/package.json pins react ^19.2.3 (react-query ^5.100.5). The react-query reasoning in §8.5 is correct either way.
findings.fix: Change the locked stack line to 'React 19 + TypeScript'.

findings.title: State 3b's premise is narrower than §8.5 implies, because linkCount counts inferred links
findings.problem: linkCount is linkedRelations.size, populated by link() for declared edges, detail-inferred edges and expanded egress alike. A failed createAllEdges on a payload whose details still yield inferences gives linkCount > 0, so a peerless resource lands in 3a - the unfounded claim 3b exists to avoid.
findings.fix: Add one sentence noting linkCount includes inferred links, so 3b catches the total-edge-failure case while 3a remains reachable on a partial one - an accepted limit, not a missed case.

findings.title: The keyed getOrCompute overload's null / no-request path is unspecified
findings.problem: keyForCurrentRequest returns the whole key, not a suffix, and returns null outside a request so caching is skipped. The design says the two-argument method delegates 'with the request-derived suffix' without saying how that suffix is derived or what the overload does with a null one.
findings.fix: State that keyForCurrentRequest splits into a nullable suffixForCurrentRequest() plus key assembly, and that the overload returns compute.get() uncached on a null suffix, preserving today's no-request behaviour. Moot if finding 6(a) is taken.
